## Overview

The "OpenTelemetry Model Forward vs Execute Time" section of `docs/design/metrics.md` says the current implementation exposes `vllm:model_forward_time_milliseconds` and `vllm:model_execute_time_milliseconds`. Neither exists in V1. This updates the section to match the code.

cc @markmc

## Claims

- The two metric names no longer appear anywhere outside `docs/`.
- The three span attributes in the section's sample trace (`gen_ai.latency.time_in_scheduler`, `time_in_model_forward`, `time_in_model_execute`) are still defined in `vllm/tracing/utils.py` but never set.
- `--collect-detailed-traces` only feeds `ObservabilityConfig.collect_model_forward_time` and `collect_model_execute_time`, which have no readers, so the flag no longer changes what is traced.
- The section now says what the V1 request span records instead (`time_in_model_prefill`, `time_in_model_decode`, `time_in_model_inference`).

Docs only, no code changes.

## Validation

On fa423b6 (main, 2026-10-05):

```console
$ git grep -n "model_forward_time_milliseconds\|model_execute_time_milliseconds" -- ':!docs/'
(no matches)

$ git grep -n "collect_model_forward_time\|collect_model_execute_time" -- ':!docs/'
vllm/config/observability.py:113:    def collect_model_forward_time(self) -> bool:
vllm/config/observability.py:121:    def collect_model_execute_time(self) -> bool:

$ git grep -n "TIME_IN_SCHEDULER\|TIME_IN_MODEL_FORWARD\|TIME_IN_MODEL_EXECUTE"
vllm/tracing/utils.py:37:    GEN_AI_LATENCY_TIME_IN_SCHEDULER = "gen_ai.latency.time_in_scheduler"
vllm/tracing/utils.py:40:    GEN_AI_LATENCY_TIME_IN_MODEL_FORWARD = "gen_ai.latency.time_in_model_forward"
vllm/tracing/utils.py:41:    GEN_AI_LATENCY_TIME_IN_MODEL_EXECUTE = "gen_ai.latency.time_in_model_execute"

$ git grep -n "SpanAttributes.GEN_AI_LATENCY" -- vllm/
vllm/v1/engine/output_processor.py:849:            SpanAttributes.GEN_AI_LATENCY_TIME_TO_FIRST_TOKEN: (
vllm/v1/engine/output_processor.py:852:            SpanAttributes.GEN_AI_LATENCY_E2E: e2e_time,
vllm/v1/engine/output_processor.py:853:            SpanAttributes.GEN_AI_LATENCY_TIME_IN_QUEUE: queued_time,
vllm/v1/engine/output_processor.py:858:            SpanAttributes.GEN_AI_LATENCY_TIME_IN_MODEL_PREFILL: prefill_time,
vllm/v1/engine/output_processor.py:859:            SpanAttributes.GEN_AI_LATENCY_TIME_IN_MODEL_DECODE: decode_time,
vllm/v1/engine/output_processor.py:860:            SpanAttributes.GEN_AI_LATENCY_TIME_IN_MODEL_INFERENCE: inference_time,
```

`pre-commit run markdownlint-cli2 --files docs/design/metrics.md` and `pre-commit run typos --files docs/design/metrics.md` pass.

## Details

I kept the section rather than deleting it, because its closing paragraph is still an open question (whether finer-grained timings are worth the overhead). The diff only changes tense and adds what V1 records today. The quoted help text is unchanged since it still matches the current docstring.

Checked for overlap with open PRs: #54830 also edits this file but only the LoRA section, and #32573 adds new tracing attributes but does not set the forward/execute ones. Neither covers this section.

If it would help, I can follow up with a PR that either deprecates `--collect-detailed-traces` or wires the timings back up, whichever maintainers prefer.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to locate the stale references and draft the wording. I reviewed every changed line and ran the commands above.

---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

@@ -670,7 +670,8 @@ fall under the more general heading of "Observability".
 vLLM has support for OpenTelemetry tracing:
 
 - Added by <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/4687> and reinstated by <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/20372>
-- Configured with `--otlp-traces-endpoint` and `--collect-detailed-traces`
+- Configured with `--otlp-traces-endpoint`. `--collect-detailed-traces` is
+  still accepted but no longer changes what is traced - see below.
 - [OpenTelemetry blog post](https://opentelemetry.io/blog/2024/llm-observability/)
 - [User-facing docs](../../examples/observability/opentelemetry/README.md)
 - [Blog post](https://medium.com/@ronen.schaffer/follow-the-trail-supercharging-vllm-with-opentelemetry-distributed-tracing-aa655229b46f)
@@ -684,23 +685,23 @@ of tracing to be quite separate from metrics.
 
 ### OpenTelemetry Model Forward vs Execute Time
 
-The current implementation exposes the following two metrics:
+The V0 engine exposed the following two metrics:
 
 - `vllm:model_forward_time_milliseconds` (Histogram) - The time spent
   in the model forward pass when this request was in the batch.
 - `vllm:model_execute_time_milliseconds` (Histogram) - The time spent
   in the model execute function. This will include model forward,
   block/sync across workers, cpu-gpu sync time and sampling time.
 
-These metrics are only enabled when OpenTelemetry tracing is enabled
-and if `--collect-detailed-traces=all/model/worker` is used. The
+These metrics were only enabled when OpenTelemetry tracing was enabled
+and if `--collect-detailed-traces=all/model/worker` was used. The
 documentation for this option states:
 
 > collect detailed traces for the specified modules. This involves
 > use of possibly costly and or blocking operations and hence might
 > have a performance impact.
 
-The metrics were added by <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/7089> and show up in an OpenTelemetry trace
+The metrics were added by <https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/7089> and showed up in an OpenTelemetry trace
 as:
 
 ```text
@@ -709,6 +710,14 @@ as:
 -> gen_ai.latency.time_in_model_execute: Double(3.6468167304992676)
 ```
 
+Neither metric exists in V1, and none of these three span attributes are
+set. `ObservabilityConfig.collect_model_forward_time` and
+`collect_model_execute_time` are still derived from
+`--collect-detailed-traces`, but nothing reads them. The V1 request span
+instead carries coarser timings computed from per-request timestamps:
+`gen_ai.latency.time_in_model_prefill`, `gen_ai.latency.time_in_model_decode`
+and `gen_ai.latency.time_in_model_inference`.
+
 We already have `inference_time` and `decode_time` metrics, so the
 question is whether there are sufficiently common use cases for the
 higher-resolution timings to justify the overhead.
